clauses.reason: The order approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act: the operative words of the President's order are "do order that the said Code of Fair Competition be and it is hereby approved with the following condition". The condition, a registration requirement for vehicles of warehousing enterprises within the code's Article II coverage, is stated as a condition of the approval and operates only through the code. An approved code had legal effect only through section 3 (under 3(b) its provisions became the standards of fair competition, under 3(c) the district courts could enjoin violations, under 3(f) violations were misdemeanors). Section 2 of S.J. Res. 113, approved June 14, 1935, provides: "All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed". The approval therefore ceased to have operative effect on June 14, 1935. No held record shows this code cancelled or suspended earlier, and June 16, 1935 is not an end because section 1 of the resolution replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936.

research_rationale:
EO 6600 was read in full in the registered APP transcription (common-crawl capture 2024-04-17T01:11:33Z). Identity: the census register row, the WPA 1944 numbered list (1934 Feb 10, p. 567, 'Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry conditionally approved') and the APP page record with the same sha256 agree on number, date and subject; the page heading names the order's number, its date matches, and the page record's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The order has one operative paragraph: it adopts the Administrator's report and findings and approves the code 'with the following condition', a registration requirement for vehicles of enterprises principally engaged in warehousing furniture and household goods that fall within Article II, Section 1, subsection A, paragraph (1) of the code. Under the shared reviewed analysis (SHARED_ANALYSIS.md, ADJUDICATION.json) a code-dependent command that did not end earlier ended on June 14, 1935, when section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 repealed the power to approve or prescribe codes and the provisions enforcing them; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded only as a validity characterization. Original not yet held; the working text is a labeled transcription under the 2026-10-21 owner ruling.

EO 6684-D (April 19, 1934) approves the Household Goods Storage and Moving Trade code, reads Article II, Section 1 of that code together with Article II, Section 1 of the Trucking Industry code, and provides for a public hearing before June 15, 1934 on whether vehicles carrying used household goods or used office furniture fall wholly or partly under the Trucking Industry code or under that code; it does not cancel or replace this approval, and the result of that hearing is not held. EO 6925 (December 19, 1934) cancels the approval of the Cinders, Ashes and Scavenger Trade code and recites 'the Code of Fair Competition for the Trucking Industry approved February 10, 1934' as the code that would then govern most of that trade's transport operations, which is consistent with this approval remaining in force on that date. No held text cites this order by number. No held record shows this code or this approval cancelled, modified under section 10(b), revoked, suspended or superseded before June 14, 1935, and the order states no period, condition or 'until' date of its own. June 16, 1935 is not an end: section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. May 27, 1935 (Schechter) is a validity characterization, not an end. savings.reason: Acts, liabilities and completed action under the code before June 14, 1935 are accrued; the section 5 exemption for past complying action is accrued; no held source continues the approval itself after the repeal.

source_notes.date_qualification: 1935-05-27: date the section 3 delegation was declared unconstitutional; validity characterization (void from issuance under then-prevailing doctrine), not an end date
source_notes.reason: Schechter held the section 3 code-making delegation unconstitutional and the code provisions there in question invalid. Recorded as a validity characterization of every section 3 approval (void from issuance under the doctrine then prevailing), not as an end of this order's command; no held record shows that the government cancelled or suspended this code on May 27, 1935.
